# Swift

The runtime (`Tabula`) and the generator's logic (`TabulaCodegen`) are done
and checked on Linux and macOS. The generator does not yet run inside a
build: the `@Machine` macro that will call it needs a SwiftPM that can declare
a macro target, which the pinned toolchain cannot. Until it lands you write
the dispatcher's shape by hand -- shown below -- and the guarantee holds the
same way, because it comes from protocol conformance, not from the macro.

## The surface the macro will read

This block is not an illustration. It is the first `swift` block of
`macros/SURFACE.md`, and a check parses it on every run with the macro's own
syntax reader, so it cannot drift from what the macro will accept:

```swift
@Machine
enum Turnstile {
    enum S { case locked, unlocked }
    enum A { case coin, push }
    enum F { case click }

    final class Ctx { var admitted = 0 }

    static let initial = S.locked

    //                        Coin                        Push
    @Row(.locked)   static let l = [ .go(.unlocked, [.click]),  .ignore ]
    @Row(.unlocked) static let u = [ .ignore,                   .handle ]

    // Carries the color and the return type. Every required member the
    // generator emits is stamped from this one line.
    func handle(_ ctx: Ctx, _ state: S, _ action: A) -> Step<S, F> { fatalError() }
}
```

<sub>From [`tabular-center-swift/macros/SURFACE.md`](https://github.com/tabula-center/tabular-center/blob/main/tabular-center-swift/macros/SURFACE.md).</sub>

## What you write today

The matrix as a `Table` literal in a `*.tb.swift` file
([why](matrix-files)):

```swift
extension Timer {
    static let TABLE = Table(
        machine: "Timer",
        states: ["Idle", "Running", "Done"],
        actions: ["Start", "Tick", "Cancel"],
        cells: [
            [.handle, .ignore, .ignore],
            [.ignore, .handle, .go(target: "Idle", effects: ["StopClock"])],
            [.go(target: "Running", effects: ["StartClock"]), .ignore, .ignore],
        ],
        initial: "Idle"
    )
}
```

<sub>From [`tabular-center-swift/examples/Sources/Timer/Timer.tb.swift`](https://github.com/tabula-center/tabular-center/blob/main/tabular-center-swift/examples/Sources/Timer/Timer.tb.swift).</sub>

One protocol requirement per `HANDLE` cell and per effect, then the
dispatcher -- the shape `TabulaCodegen` emits and the macro will generate. The
`switch` has no `default:`, so a new state or action breaks it:

```swift
    protocol Cells {
        func idleStart(_ ctx: Ctx) -> Step<S, F>
        func runningTick(_ ctx: Ctx, _ state: Running, _ action: Tick) -> Step<S, F>
        func startClock(_ ctx: Ctx) -> A?
        func stopClock(_ ctx: Ctx, _ reason: Reason) -> A?
    }
```

<sub>From [`tabular-center-swift/examples/Sources/Timer/Timer.swift`](https://github.com/tabula-center/tabular-center/blob/main/tabular-center-swift/examples/Sources/Timer/Timer.swift).</sub>

```swift
    static func step(_ c: Cells, _ ctx: Ctx, _ s: S, _ a: A) -> Step<S, F> {
        switch (s, a) {
        case (.idle, .start): return c.idleStart(ctx)
        case (.idle, .tick): return .ignored
        case (.idle, .cancel): return .ignored
        case (.running, .start): return .ignored
        case let (.running(since), .tick(now)):
            return c.runningTick(ctx, Running(since: since), Tick(now: now))
        case (.running, .cancel):
            return .go(.idle, effects: [.stopClock(reason: .cancelled)])
        case (.done, .start): return .go(.running(since: 0), effects: [.startClock])
        case (.done, .tick): return .ignored
        case (.done, .cancel): return .ignored
        }
    }
```

<sub>From [`tabular-center-swift/examples/Sources/Timer/Timer.swift`](https://github.com/tabula-center/tabular-center/blob/main/tabular-center-swift/examples/Sources/Timer/Timer.swift).</sub>

Then the implementation, with narrowed arguments -- `state.since` and
`action.now` are plain fields:

```swift
    struct Impl: Cells {
        func idleStart(_ ctx: Ctx) -> Step<S, F> {
            .go(.running(since: 0), effects: [.startClock])
        }

        func runningTick(_ ctx: Ctx, _ state: Running, _ action: Tick) -> Step<S, F> {
            // No `if case`, no cast, no force-unwrap: the dispatcher matched.
            if action.now - state.since >= ctx.limit {
                return .go(.done, effects: [.stopClock(reason: .elapsed)])
            }
            // Handled, and staying put. Distinct from `.ignored`, which would
            // claim a tick is meaningless while running.
            return .stay(effects: [])
        }

        func startClock(_ ctx: Ctx) -> A? {
            ctx.log.append("start")
            return nil
        }

        func stopClock(_ ctx: Ctx, _ reason: Reason) -> A? {
            ctx.log.append("stop:\(reason)")
            return nil
        }
    }
```

<sub>From [`tabular-center-swift/examples/Sources/Timer/Timer.swift`](https://github.com/tabula-center/tabular-center/blob/main/tabular-center-swift/examples/Sources/Timer/Timer.swift).</sub>

## When a cell is missing

```text
error: does not conform to protocol
```

swiftc's own conformance error, required by a fixture on every run. The
dispatcher has no `default:`, and neither does your code, which is where one
would otherwise creep in.

## Colors, SwiftUI, and pinning a matrix

- **Colors.** A prototype marked `async`, `throws`, `@MainActor` or any other
  attribute is copied onto every generated member, and callers get
  `try await` where the color demands it. A colored child under an uncolored
  parent does not compile.
- **`ObservableStore`** is a `@MainActor` store SwiftUI can observe (macOS 14,
  iOS 17), written without the `@Observable` macro so the runtime asks nothing
  of macro plugins. `Store` and `AsyncStore` work everywhere.
- **`TabulaTesting`** parses a `.tbl` fixture and diffs it against a machine's
  `TABLE` -- a reviewable, one-line-per-row pin of the matrix:

```swift
    static let FIXTURE = """
        machine Turnstile
        initial Locked
        states  Locked Unlocked
        actions Coin Push

        Locked   | GO(Unlocked) | IGNORE
        Unlocked | IGNORE       | HANDLE
        """
```

<sub>From [`tabular-center-swift/examples/Sources/SpecCheck/Turnstile.swift`](https://github.com/tabula-center/tabular-center/blob/main/tabular-center-swift/examples/Sources/SpecCheck/Turnstile.swift).</sub>

```swift
do {
    let spec = try parseSpec(Turnstile.FIXTURE, "Turnstile.FIXTURE")
    Check.eq(
        checkTable(Turnstile.TABLE, spec),
        [],
        "spec: the matrix matches the fixture a reviewer reads")

    // And it notices when they disagree. One cell changed from HANDLE to
    // GO(Locked) -- a difference that compiles, passes every behavioural test
    // that does not exercise that cell, and is exactly what a table diff is
    // for.
    let drifted = try parseSpec(Turnstile.DRIFTED, "Turnstile.DRIFTED")
    let differences = checkTable(Turnstile.TABLE, drifted)
    Check.ok(!differences.isEmpty, "spec: a changed cell is reported, not shrugged at")
    Check.ok(
        differences.count == 1,
        "spec: one changed cell is one difference, not a cascade")
} catch {
    Check.ok(false, "spec: the fixture failed to parse: \(error)")
}
```

<sub>From [`tabular-center-swift/examples/Sources/SpecCheck/main.swift`](https://github.com/tabula-center/tabular-center/blob/main/tabular-center-swift/examples/Sources/SpecCheck/main.swift).</sub>

The package declares `swift-tools-version: 5.9` and no `platforms:` clause, so
it asks nothing of a deployment target; only `ObservableStore` carries an
`@available`.

## Examples

In [`tabular-center-swift/examples`](https://github.com/tabula-center/tabular-center/blob/main/tabular-center-swift/examples), one executable target each:

| | | adds |
|---|---|---|
| 1-4 | `TrafficLight`, `Timer`, `Retry`, `Login` | the four core machines |
| 6 | `ObservableCounter` | `ObservableStore`; skips, saying so, where Observation is absent |
| 7 | `SpecCheck` | `TabulaTesting`, matching and then deliberately mismatching |
